title: Ask the old guard
translation: Major Counsellor Mitsutada, who later became a monk, was to lead the New Year's Eve ceremony for driving out demons. He asked the Tōin Minister of the Right to take him through it step by step. The answer: "You can't do better than taking Matagorō as your teacher."

Matagorō was an old palace guard who knew every court ceremony inside out. Once, when Lord Konoe took his seat for a ceremony, he forgot the kneeling mat and called straight for the secretary. Matagorō was there tending the fire, and he muttered, very quietly: "Perhaps you might call for the kneeling mat first, sir?"
original: {尹|いんの}{大納言|だいなごん}{光忠|みつただ}{入道|にふだう}、{追儺|ついな}の{上卿|しやうけい}を{務|つと}められけるに、{洞院|とうゐん}{右大臣殿|うだいじんどの}に{次第|しだい}を{申|まう}し{請|う}けられければ、
「{又五郎|またごらう}をのこを{師|し}とするより{外|ほか}の{才覚|さいかく}{候|さうら}はじ。」とぞ{宣|のたま}ひける。
かの{又五郎|またごらう}は{老|お}いたる{衛士|ゑじ}の、よく{公事|くじ}に{馴|な}れたる{者|もの}にてぞありける。
{近衛殿|このゑどの}{著陣|ちやくぢん}したまひける{時|とき}、{膝突|ひざつき}をわすれて、{外記|げき}をめされければ、
{火|ひ}たきて{候|さうら}ひけるが、「まづ{膝突|ひざつき}をめさるべくや{候|さうらふ}らむ。」と、{忍|しの}びやかにつぶやきける、いとをかしかりけり。
literal: When the lay monk Mitsutada, the Censor Major Counsellor, was to serve as the noble in charge of the demon-expelling rite, and asked the Tōin Minister of the Right for the order of proceedings,
he said, 'There can be no better plan than to take the fellow Matagorō as your teacher.'
That Matagorō was an old guard, a man well used to court ceremonies.
When Lord Konoe took his seat in the guards' hall, he forgot the kneeling mat and called for the secretary;
(Matagorō), who was in attendance tending the fire, muttered quietly, 'Should you not perhaps first call for the kneeling mat?': that was very delightful.

notes.text: {尹|いん}: head of the Board of Censors ({弾正台|だんじやうだい}), a post that by this time was mostly an honour. He had also been a major counsellor and then became a lay monk ({入道|にふだう}). Commentators identify him as Minamoto no Mitsutada, who held these posts around 1330. Kenkō calls him by the title he had when writing. The 1925 edition gives the reading いんの.

{追儺|ついな}: the rite on the last night of the year in which a masked man and his helpers chased the demons of disease out of the palace. Today's {節分|せつぶん}, when people throw beans to drive out demons, comes from it.
{上卿|しやうけい}: the senior noble in charge of a court ceremony. The 1925 edition gives the reading しやうけい.
Commentators differ: either Tōin Kinkata, or his father Tōin Saneyasu (if 右 'right' is a slip for 左 'left'). A minister, and he sends the counsellor to an old guard.

{衛士|ゑじ}: guards sent up from the provinces to the capital for a term of service. They kept watch at the palace gates and tended the fires at night, which is why Matagorō is there, tending the fire, when the mistake happens.

notes.quote: 近衛殿著陣したまひける時
notes.text: {近衛殿|このゑどの}: a head of the Konoe family, one of the families that supplied the regents. Commentators disagree on which one. {著陣|ちやくぢん}: to take one's seat in the guards' hall ({陣|ぢん}), where nobles met to do government business.
{膝突|ひざつき}: a small mat put down for an official to kneel on when he came forward to hand over or receive documents. It had to be laid before the secretary was called.

notes.quote: まづ膝突をめさるべくや候らむ
notes.text: Very polite and very indirect: べく 'should', や … らむ 'might it be that…?', and {候|さうらふ} for respect. The low-ranking guard corrects one of the highest nobles at court without seeming to.
